'''Oxana Vasilievna Kharissova''' (born 1969) is a Ukrainian–Mexican [[nanoscience|nanoscientist]] whose research involves the [[Chemical synthesis|synthesis]] and [[solubility]] of [[nanoparticle]]s.{{r|apasionada}} She is a professor and researcher in the faculty of physical and mathematical sciences at the [[Autonomous University of Nuevo León]].{{r|uanl}}

==Education and career==
Kharissova was born in 1969 in Ukraine, then part of the [[Soviet Union]].{{r|achh}} She earned a bachelor's degree in [[geochemistry]] in 1993 and a master's degree in [[crystallography]] in 1994, both from [[Moscow State University]],{{r|apasionada}} before emigrating to Mexico in 1995 and later becoming a Mexican citizen in 2004.{{r|achh}} She has a 2001 Ph.D. in [[materials science]] from the Autonomous University of Nuevo León, where she is a professor and researcher.{{r|apasionada}}

==Books==
Kharissova is a co-author or co-editor of books including:
*''Handbook of Less-Common Nanostructures'' (with Boris I. Kharisov and Ubaldo Ortiz-Mendez, CRC Press, 2012)
*''Solubilization and Dispersion of Carbon Nanotubes'' (with Boris I. Kharisov, Springer, 2017)
*''Carbon Allotropes: Metal-Complex Chemistry, Properties and Applications'' (with Boris I. Kharisov, Springer, 2019){{r|ca}}

==Recognition==
Kharissova is a member of the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]],{{r|amc}} elected in 2010.{{r|uanl}} In 2017 the Autonomous University of Nuevo León gave her their "Flama, Vida y Mujer" recognition, in the area of teaching and research.{{r|fvm}}
